anchor.quote: Identify user needs

not_rules.note: Advice to the writer about conducting user research (G-5).

anchor.quote: Engage Easy Read experts

not_rules.note: Advice to project team / writer on procuring expertise (G-5).

anchor.quote: Design and publish materials to download

not_rules.note: Grouping heading for publishing and print/accessibility considerations (G-1).

anchor.quote: Make Easy Read materials available in addition to any source material they are derived from. Publish them in HTML and as an accessible PDF at the same time as the source material.

not_rules.note: Publishing workflow advice rather than text checker rule (G-5).

anchor.quote: Users need to be able to print or download the Easy Read version from the same site as the source material.

not_rules.note: Information architecture / web publishing advice (G-5).

anchor.quote: Follow W3C updates on making content usable for people with cognitive and learning disabilities.

not_rules.note: General professional development advice (G-5).

anchor.quote: Make the structure of Easy Read PDFs accessible to help people who will need to download them from the website.

not_rules.note: Covered under general PDF and accessibility standards pages (G-6).

anchor.quote: Make all government content accessible to people with disability. This includes providing information that is timely, which is part of Australian law under the Disability Discrimination Act 1992.

not_rules.note: Legal compliance statement / general advice (G-5).

anchor.quote: Plan the structure

not_rules.note: Process guidance on drafting and structural planning (G-5).

anchor.quote: Keep text simple

not_rules.note: Grouping heading for text level and vocabulary (G-1).

anchor.quote: If you have defined a lot of words, include a glossary at the end of your document. Call it a word list.

not_rules.note: Conditional structural advice; also restated under Provide context (G-4, G-5).

anchor.quote: If you need information from people, follow questions with practical examples so people know how to respond. Ask your Easy Read professional to help you design these materials.

not_rules.note: Content design advice (G-5).

anchor.quote: Involve others as you draft

not_rules.note: Process and stakeholder engagement advice (G-5).

anchor.quote: Keep your Easy Read brief. This is not always possible for complex information. In that case, think about whether you can divide the content into a few documents. Check if this decision will meet user needs.

not_rules.note: General editorial guidance (G-5).

anchor.quote: Content that you create as part of your work for the Australian Government is a record. Records provide evidence of what your organisation has done and why.

not_rules.note: Information management background explanation (G-5).

anchor.quote: Managing and disposing of records is required under the Archives Act 1983. For guidance, visit the National Archives of Australia’s information management standards.

not_rules.note: Regulatory guidance and link to external standards (G-5).

anchor.quote: Follow a standard Easy Read layout

not_rules.note: Grouping heading for layout and typography specifications (G-1).

anchor.quote: Tables help to align images and words. If you use them, follow accessibility requirements for tables. When designing the Easy Read material, code tables using the role="presentation" attribute.

not_rules.note: Accessibility coding practice for HTML/PDF covered in tables/accessibility pages (G-6).

anchor.quote: Use wide margins and plenty of white space to make the text easy to read.

not_rules.note: Unquantified visual design guidance (G-5).

anchor.quote: Be careful using text effects – any change to the shape of letters makes them more difficult to read.

not_rules.note: General advisory note to the designer/writer (G-5).

anchor.quote: Use colour and contrast to make words stand out, but don’t rely on colour to convey meaning.

not_rules.note: Standard WCAG rule covered on colour/accessibility pages (G-6).

anchor.quote: Use matte paper stock: it reduces glare off the page.

not_rules.note: Physical print procurement specification, not text (G-5).

not_rules.note: Guidance on what editorial sections/information to provide at the beginning and end of content (G-5).

not_rules.quote: Provide context

covers.quote: provide clear link text and make sure it looks like a link

rules.quote: spell out the URL next to the linked text.
rules.violation_condition: a hyperlink in an Easy Read document whose destination URL is not explicitly spelled out adjacent to the link text
when: In Easy Read materials containing hyperlinks.
rules.why: G-2 consolidates link formatting requirements under Print considerations into one checker rule.

covers.quote: Use simple words and grammar, but don’t use childish language if the users are adults.

rules.quote: Check your content reads between a year 4 to year 6 reading level.
rules.violation_condition: Easy Read content with a reading level score higher than year 6 (or lower than year 4)
when: When authoring Easy Read materials.
rules.why: Specific, actionable reading level instruction for Easy Read text.

covers.quote: Define the difficult word in the next sentence or phrase.
A difficult word might have 3 or more syllables.

examples.note: A difficult word is introduced and defined immediately in subsequent sentences.

parts.quote: Immunisation protects your baby from some diseases. Immunisation means a doctor or nurse gives your baby a needle with a vaccineinside. The vaccine is the medicine that protects your baby from some diseases.

rules.quote: If you need to use a difficult word, write it in bold.
rules.specification: A difficult word is defined as having 3 or more syllables; when used, it must be bolded and defined immediately afterwards.
rules.violation_condition: a difficult word (e.g. 3 or more syllables) in Easy Read text that is not set in bold or not followed by a definition in the next sentence or phrase
when: When using a difficult word (defined in the manual as typically having 3 or more syllables) in Easy Read content.
rules.why: G-2 combines styling and defining difficult words into one rule.

rules.quote: Only use questions in headings for Easy Read.
rules.violation_condition: a question (sentence ending with a question mark) appearing in the body text rather than a heading in Easy Read content
when: In Easy Read text.
rules.why: G-4 prefers the explicit instruction in prose over the candidate heading.

rules.violation_condition: Easy Read body text formatted with line spacing less than 1.5
when: In Easy Read layouts.
rules.why: Explicit typographic rule.

covers.quote: Don’t put images above the text or vice versa.

rules.quote: If you’re using images, place them on the left to align with the text on the right.
rules.violation_condition: images placed above, below, or to the right of text rather than on the left aligned with text on the right
when: When layout includes images in Easy Read content.
rules.why: G-2 folds the negative instruction into the primary layout rule.

rules.violation_condition: text that is justified, centred, or right-aligned instead of left-aligned
when: In Easy Read text formatting.
rules.why: Clear formatting rule for Easy Read.

rules.quote: Use at least size 14 font for text and a larger size for headings.
rules.violation_condition: body text smaller than 14pt/14px, or headings not larger than the body text size
when: In Easy Read text formatting.
rules.why: Explicit typographical rule for minimum font size.

rules.quote: Only use bold for headings and difficult words.
rules.violation_condition: bold formatting applied to text that is neither a heading nor a defined difficult word
when: In Easy Read text formatting.
rules.why: Clear restrictive typographic rule.

rules.quote: Don’t split paragraphs and sentences across pages in print and PDF documents.
rules.violation_condition: a sentence or paragraph broken across a page break in print or PDF Easy Read documents
when: In print and PDF Easy Read documents.
rules.why: Direct layout constraint for PDF/print pagination.

rules.quote: Insert page numbers in print and PDF documents, in the same font size as your text.
rules.violation_condition: a print or PDF Easy Read document lacking page numbers, or having page numbers formatted in a font size different from the body text
when: In print and PDF Easy Read documents.
rules.why: Direct pagination rule specifying presence and font size.

rules.quote: Include your agency or department logo on the cover page only.
rules.violation_condition: an agency or department logo appearing on pages other than the cover page in an Easy Read document
when: In Easy Read publications with agency or department logos.
rules.why: Explicit document layout restriction.
